ai.title: codebuff replaces manicode in npm package identity
ai.summary: The npm package name and bin entry in `npm-app/package.json` changed from `manicode` to `codebuff`. Version remains `1.0.99`. This aligns the CLI binary with the new branding. Existing installs of `manicode` will not auto-update to the `codebuff` package.

eli5.text: The assistant's downloadable package for developers and the command used to run it from a terminal have both been renamed from 'manicode' to 'codebuff'. This only affects people who installed the tool before; anyone downloading it fresh will get the new name, and existing installs won't switch over automatically.

ai.title: Switch haiku constant to 3.5 and update request-files model
ai.summary: The `claudeModels.haiku` constant in `common/src/constants.ts` is updated from `claude-3-haiku-20240307` to `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022`. Consequently, `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` now invoke this new Haiku 3.5 model for file request generation and session initialization, replacing the previous Sonnet usage. Cost tracking in `backend/src/billing/message-cost-tracker.ts` reflects the new model's pricing, with input tokens rising from 0.25 to 1.0 and output from 1.25 to 5.0 per million.

eli5.text: The assistant now uses Claude's faster, more affordable 3.5 Haiku model instead of the larger Sonnet model to figure out which files you need when you start a new task. Because Haiku 3.5 costs more to run, the per-token pricing that gets tracked in your usage bill has gone up for this part of the work. If you watched the backend logs during a session startup, you'd see file-request calls tagged with the new Haiku 3.5 identifier instead of Sonnet. This affects only the file-discovery step of new sessions and is live today.

ai.title: Filter null content in file version updates
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts now filters null content from readFilesPaths before calling getRelevantFileInfoMessage in getFileVersionUpdates. Prevents invalid paths with null content from triggering file info messages. Scope limited to backend prompt logic.

eli5.text: The assistant now skips over files that have no readable content when it checks whether a file's contents have changed, so you won't get a confusing message about a file that isn't actually available. This is live today and applies only to the backend logic that manages file-version comparisons.

ai.title: Refine file-request prompts
ai.summary: Updated backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts to clarify Haiku's file-selection tasks. Replaced 'Ignore previous instructions' with explicit context and added strict output constraints. Prevents model confusion and ensures relevant file retrieval.

eli5.text: The internal system that picks out which files the assistant reads has been told to do its job more carefully. Instead of asking the assistant to ignore earlier guidance and figure out the task on its own, the system now spells out the task in plain terms and asks for a very specific output: just the file names, nothing else. The system now also tells the assistant up front that it is selecting relevant files and that broad requests may need a lot of files. If you never looked at this part, you wouldn't notice this change, but anyone paying attention to how the assistant chooses files will see it sticking to the right ones instead of getting confused by mixed messages.

ai.title: Switch file rewrite fallback to Claude Haiku
ai.summary: File rewrite fallback in `processFileBlock` now uses `claudeModels.haiku` via `promptClaude` instead of `openaiModels.gpt4o` via `promptOpenAI`. This change is internal to the backend file processing logic, specifically affecting how failed diff applications are retried. Scope is limited to `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` and associated imports from `common/constants`. The prompt structure remains identical, only the underlying model provider and specific model identifier change.

eli5.text: When the assistant fails to apply a code edit exactly as written, it now retries using a different AI model (Anthropic's Claude Haiku) instead of OpenAI's GPT-4o. This only affects the behind-the-scenes backend system that corrects failed edits, not the main chat experience. No visible change for end users - it's internal housekeeping to potentially improve edit retry reliability.
